facts.text: The Al0.7CoCrFeNi eutectic high-entropy alloy was subjected to high-pressure, high-temperature treatment in a hexahedron-anvil apparatus.
The HPHT treatment pressure was 6 GPa.
The HPHT treatment temperature was 1473 K.
The alloy was held under the HPHT conditions for 2 hours before cooling and decompression.
HPHT treatment transformed the dual-phase lamellar microstructure into a hierarchically patterned microstructure with coherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
The coherent interfaces promoted preferential dislocation transfer from the softer FCC phase into the harder B2 phase.
Dislocation transfer across the coherent FCC/B2 interfaces relieved interfacial stress concentrations.
The hierarchical microstructure activated dislocations, stacking faults, microbands, and twins, producing a more homogeneous strain distribution.
Relative to the conventional homogenized baseline, HPHT treatment simultaneously increased tensile strength and ductility by nearly 100%.
The HPHT-treated alloy reached a fracture strength of approximately 1150 MPa.
The HPHT-treated alloy reached approximately 36% uniform tensile elongation.
HPHT treatment changed fracture behavior from catastrophic interfacial cracking to distributed, isolated microcracking.
